description: Post-resolution first-wins dedup for the clause's named example, mo resolving to loaded ro. Loads ro and en with fallback en; no mo catalog exists, so every mo observation is resolution behavior rather than loading behavior. localeFallbackCandidates (DefaultStrings.java:2474-2503) builds the raw candidate set for mo as [mo, ro, en]: CldrLocaleData.fallbackLocalesFor(mo) is [mo, ro], the likely-subtag match for ro-Latn re-adds ro, the auto-identity tiebreaker DefaultStrings installs for language code 'ro' re-adds it again, and the fallback locale is appended at 2489. Dedup happens AFTER each raw candidate is resolved to a catalog by localizedStringsFor (2506) - canonicalLanguageTag('mo') is 'ro', so mo maps onto loaded ro - and the putIfAbsent at 2498 is keyed by that RESOLVED attempted locale, so the walk sees two candidates, not three. Dedup.Shared exists in both catalogs to show which one first-wins keeps. Dedup.ResolutionFailure is a cardinality placeholder over the context name 'absentCount', which no case supplies, so ro throws IllegalArgumentException at DefaultStrings.java:966-968 while the same key is a plain string in en; that pair makes policy truncation visible against a reachable translation. Its ro translations declare Romanian's complete cardinality set (one/few/other) so the load emits no warning and the fixture isolates exactly one failure cause. Dedup.Missing exists nowhere. Loaded ro and en have distinct language codes, so no tiebreakers are required.
